source: Ten usability heuristics for user interface design by Jakob Nielsen. Descriptions are ours.

heuristics.name: Visibility of system status
heuristics.description: The product should always show what's going on: loading, saved, failed.
heuristics.apply: After each action, check the page shows whether it's working, done or failed.

heuristics.name: Match with the real world
heuristics.description: Words and ordering should be the user's, not the system's internal terms.
heuristics.apply: Read labels and messages for jargon, internal codes or ordering a user wouldn't expect.

heuristics.name: User control and freedom
heuristics.description: Users need a clear way out: cancel, close, undo, back.
heuristics.apply: In every dialog, form and multi-step flow, look for a way to leave without harm.

heuristics.name: Consistency and standards
heuristics.description: The same thing should look and work the same everywhere, and follow platform conventions.
heuristics.apply: Compare how similar controls, words and actions behave on different pages.

heuristics.name: Error prevention
heuristics.description: Good design stops mistakes before they happen, for example by disabling invalid choices or confirming risky ones.
heuristics.apply: Try to make a mistake the design could have prevented, like submitting an obviously wrong value.

heuristics.name: Recognition rather than recall
heuristics.description: Users shouldn't have to remember information from one screen to use on another.
heuristics.apply: Look for steps that need something the user saw earlier but can no longer see.

heuristics.name: Flexibility and efficiency
heuristics.description: Frequent users should have shortcuts, while new users can still find their way.
heuristics.apply: Check for shortcuts (keyboard, search, defaults) in frequent tasks.

heuristics.name: Minimalist design
heuristics.description: Every extra piece of information competes with the relevant ones.
heuristics.apply: Look for pages where clutter hides the main action or information.

heuristics.name: Help users recover from errors
heuristics.description: Error messages should be plain, point at the problem and suggest a fix.
heuristics.apply: Cause input errors and check the message says what's wrong and how to fix it, next to the field.

heuristics.name: Help and documentation
heuristics.description: Help should be easy to find, focused on the task and short.
heuristics.apply: Look for help where users are likely to need it, and check it matches what the product does.
